title: Allowing Makers to Adopt Certain Markings for National Firearms Act Firearms

Lawful gun owners across the country will agree this rule change is a good step in the right direction.

Allowing makers to adopt existing serial numbers and manufacturer markings would reduce unnecessary costs and logistical burdens, particularly the need for specialized engraving services, without meaningfully affecting traceability or law enforcement effectiveness. The existing manufacturer markings already provide a reliable basis for tracing firearms...

The biggest reason is the engraving is hard to do on one's own, and it added even more expense when the $200 tax was in place. Now, the $200 is removed from a Form 1 submission, but we still have to pay someone to engrave the firearm after the fact. The net effect is that there's still a form of "tax" on registering an NFA firearm with the ATF....

I support this rule change in all respects. These markings can be easily used by the ATF to link the firearm to its NFA registration, should the need ever arise. Adding additional markings for the maker's name and location do not enhance the ATF's ability to identify the firearm's registered owner. This is especially true if the maker transfers the firearm...
I think the idea of removing the requirement for adding your info to an existing receiver when you form 1 SBR/ SBS it is due time for being be done. I ABSOLUTELY 100% supporting this rule change.

Please add language to make this change retro active and advise that BATFE Agents / Law Enforcement will not be required to check for markings for Tax stamps issued prior to the change going into effect. I suggest this because I can see the potential for cases where: 1. Individuals may not have been fully aware, or misunderstood the marking requirements....
This is a step in the right direction. Requireing an additional marks on a already made firearm is a good move.

If someone applying as a maker for an SBR, it would be really nice if they didn't have to do anything to the weapon other than build it. Please make it so that you (the ATF) implement this already as you already allow for a variance for people who ask.

This rule will have the public adopt NFA items more easier by simplifying the process. I have thought about getting an SBR but the issue with dealing with having to get more engraving seems like another barrier to entry. Removing it does make me want to get an SBR but until then it is still a bother

I think this is a very common sense approach to form 1 applications. I always considered the additional making requirements to be unnecessary and to cause confusion relating to which markings were valid.

This is a good rule that will benefit everyone by removing a legal requirement for modification that is typically done by a professional for a fee. And will prevent confusion when markings must be examined by law enforcement for any situation they would have legal authority to do so.

Adding a second marking to a firearm incurs a financial cost, delay and provides no advantage as the firearm already has a manufactures serial number. This only serves to burden the user! It can also destroy the value of a firearm and actually may make tracking even harder. It should be removed.
I support the removal of the engraving requirements. Utilizing the existing manufacturer engravings will simplify the process for the end user and eliminate the potential for errors.

I am echoing quite a few comments here when I say this is definitely a step in the right direction. It reduces significant unnecessary burden while preserving the value of some very rare, expensive, and collectible firearms. Requiring a secondary marking was absolutely redundant and punitive. I encourage the ATF to adopt this proposed rule (1140-AA70). The marking requirement adds extra burden and cost to people "making" a firearm on a Form1. When "making" from an existing firearm, unique and identifiable markings already exist on the host firearm. By having the Form1 applicant engrave additional identifying information is completely redundant....
The current process is over burdensome, redundant, and unnecessary. This change addresses this issue and is long overdue.
I completely support this common sense rule change to not require further engraving of already serialized firearms.
I support this rule change. Engraving and laser costs are an undue expense that should not be required to exercise your rights.
It's good that the ATF has finally started removing unnecessary administrative burden on lawful gun owners and stopped trying to gotcha them with bizarre changes.
Very pleased with the reduction in redundant adminstrative burden and cost that adds nothing to public saftey. Good change.
Shouldn't need to remark guns that already are serialized. Removing the engraving would be a nice change on sbrs

This is a step in the right direction. Persons making a SBR or SBS from an already serialized firearm may not have a local service to add additional markings that are not necessary. Additionally adding expenses to a unnecessary modern firearm conversion to have that done.

Engraving your name, city and state was so unnecessary and redundant and frankly it demolishes the resale value of the firearm should you ever want to deregister your SBR back into a pistol and/or sell it. With that said, this is a big win for stamp collectors and it's a lot less of a burden for third party engravers and firearm owners themselves....
